Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test asserts
  - testLANG_831 calls testSdfAndFdp("M E", "3  Tue", true). With shouldFail = true, both SimpleDateFormat (SDF) and FastDateParser (FDP) are expected to fail parsing the input. SDF does fail because the pattern "M E" has a single space while the input has two spaces. FDP, however, succeeds, triggering the test failure (“Expected FDF failure, but got ...”).

- How FDP builds its parsing regex
  - FastDateParser.parse uses a precompiled regex (parsePattern) to match the input (parse(...), lines 274–291).
  - parsePattern is constructed in init() by tokenizing the format string with formatPattern (lines 115–150). The pattern regex is:
    - formatPattern = "D+|E+|F+|G+|H+|K+|M+|S+|W+|Z+|a+|d+|h+|k+|m+|s+|w+|y+|z+|''|'[^']++(''[^']*+)*+'|[^'A-Za-z]++"
    - This splits "M E" into three tokens: "M", " " (a single space), and "E". The "[^'A-Za-z]++" branch ensures the literal space becomes its own token.
  - getStrategy(formatField) assigns strategies for tokens (lines 543–600):
    - "M" -> NUMBER_MONTH_STRATEGY (length 1, line 565)
    - "E" -> DAY_OF_WEEK_STRATEGY (line 555)
    - " " (a literal) -> CopyQuotedStrategy (default branch, lines 550–552)
  - For each token, addRegex appends to the regex and, if it represents a date field, returns true so it’s added to the strategies collector (lines 138–146). Literals like spaces return false but still contribute to the regex.
  - CopyQuotedStrategy.addRegex calls escapeRegex(regex, formatField, true) and returns false (lines 631–635), so the literal is included in the regex but not captured.

- Where the behavior diverges from SDF
  - The bug arises in how the literal space is escaped into the regex. The issue report states FDP “treats a single white-space as being any number of white-space characters.” This means escapeRegex turns a single space in the pattern into a regex like \s+ (or \s*), permitting multiple spaces.
  - Consequently, the compiled parsePattern for "M E" accepts inputs with two spaces, such as "3  Tue", whereas SDF requires exactly one space and fails.
  - parse(...) then matches and extracts fields via matcher.group(i), producing a valid Date for FDP, while SDF throws an exception. The test detects the inconsistency and fails.

- Summary of root cause
  - Literal whitespace in the format string is not treated literally by FastDateParser. In CopyQuotedStrategy.addRegex, the escaping routine expands a single space into a regex that matches variable amounts of whitespace. This makes FDP more permissive than SDF for whitespace, directly causing testLANG_831 to fail.

- Likely fix area
  - Adjust the escaping of literals (specifically whitespace) so that a single space in the pattern matches exactly one space in the input, consistent with SimpleDateFormat. This behavior is controlled by the method invoked from CopyQuotedStrategy.addRegex, i.e., the escaping routine that transforms literal tokens into their regex form.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

I will look up the implementation of the escaping routine used by CopyQuotedStrategy to see how whitespace is converted into regex, which likely causes the bug.
